title: Chadolbaegi with Scallion-Soy Dipping Sauce
shortDescription: Paper-thin beef brisket grilled without marinade and served with a bright scallion-soy, rice-vinegar, garlic, and sesame dipping sauce.
culturalContext: Chadolbaegi is very thinly sliced beef brisket cooked rapidly at the grill, commonly without a sweet marinade. Dipping sauces vary; the scallion-soy sauce here is a defined pairing for this guide rather than a claim of one mandatory restaurant formula.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.item: paper-thin sliced beef brisket for Korean BBQ
ingredients.preparation: kept refrigerated and separated into loose slices

marinadeOrSeasoning.meatWeightCovered: Serves alongside 680 g / 1.5 lb paper-thin beef brisket
mixOrder: Whisk soy sauce, water, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and gochugaru if using.
Stir in scallions, garlic, and sesame seeds immediately before serving.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: No marination; prepare sauce in a clean serving bowl and keep beef refrigerated separately
marinadeOrSeasoning.refrigeratedMarinationTimeRange: No marination; keep beef at 40°F / 4°C or below until grilling
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: The dipping sauce is a ready-to-eat item and must remain completely separate from raw beef, raw tongs, and the raw-meat platter.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard any portion contaminated by raw beef or raw utensils; do not combine individual used dipping bowls back into the serving bowl.
substitutions: Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce after label review.
Finely sliced mild onion may replace half the scallion, changing the flavor.
allergenNotes: Regular soy sauce usually contains wheat.

instructions.heading: Make the clean dipping sauce
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce, water, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and optional gochugaru. Stir in scallions, garlic, and sesame seeds; divide into individual bowls.
instructions.temperature: Refrigerate if held longer than 30 minutes
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sugar is dissolved and scallions remain crisp and bright.
instructions.safetyNote: Prepare the sauce before handling raw beef and keep it outside the raw-meat work zone.

instructions.heading: Separate the chilled slices
instructions.action: With clean raw-meat tongs, loosen the paper-thin brisket slices onto a raw-meat platter; keep chilled until the grill is ready.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are loose rather than frozen in a solid block and remain cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not place ready-to-eat scallions or sauce on the raw-beef platter.

instructions.heading: Preheat the approved grill
instructions.action: Heat a clean grill to medium-high. Because brisket releases fat, keep the grease channel or drip tray installed exactly as the manufacturer directs.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A slice begins sizzling immediately without uncontrolled smoking.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only an appliance approved for the location; maintain ventilation and never improvise with an indoor fuel-burning stove.

instructions.heading: Grill a few slices at a time
instructions.action: Lay slices flat without overlapping and turn after the first side browns, about 30 to 60 seconds per side depending on thickness.
instructions.temperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical folded portion, then rest 3 minutes
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Fat renders, edges brown, and no raw-looking areas remain; a practical folded sample reaches target temperature.
instructions.safetyNote: Time is only an estimate. Use separate clean cooked-food tongs and do not let raw tongs touch the dipping sauce.

instructions.heading: Manage grease safely
instructions.action: Between batches, follow the appliance manual for grease control; stop and cool the unit before emptying any tray.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Fat drains normally without overflow, flare, or heavy smoke.
instructions.safetyNote: Never pour water onto hot grease or move a hot grease tray; stop cooking if the manufacturer’s limits are exceeded.

instructions.heading: Rest and dip
instructions.action: Move cooked brisket to a clean platter, rest at least 3 minutes, and serve with individual bowls of scallion-soy sauce.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are browned, flexible, and lightly crisp at some edges.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not return used sauce to the shared bowl; discard sauce contaminated by raw utensils.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Fat is rendered and edges are browned while slices remain flexible.
A thick practical folded sample reaches 145°F / 63°C before the 3-minute rest.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Ask for Korean BBQ chadolbaegi; generic sandwich brisket is cooked/cured and is not an equivalent raw grilling cut.
Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce after label review, but sesame remains present.
ingredientSourcing: Purchase raw paper-thin sliced brisket labeled for Korean BBQ from a trusted butcher or Korean market.
Keep frozen packages frozen until refrigerator thawing; reject torn or leaking packages.
makeAhead: Prepare the sauce up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate; stir in scallions shortly before serving. Thaw frozen chadolbaegi in the refrigerator, never on the counter.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Reheat cooked brisket to 165°F / 74°C and use in a rice bowl. Discard individual dipping sauce after service rather than storing it.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice, crisp lettuce, and banchan that can cut through the brisket’s richness.
Give each diner a separate sauce bowl to reduce cross-contact at the table.

faq.question: Does chadolbaegi need a marinade?
faq.answer: No. The thin, fatty brisket is commonly grilled without marinade; this recipe puts seasoning in a separate dipping sauce.

faq.question: How can I check such thin beef with a thermometer?
faq.answer: Cook a small folded or naturally thicker sample and measure its center with a thin-tip calibrated thermometer, while also ensuring no raw-looking areas remain.
